x: The first race to be decided was the 440yds. J.
The 440 Yards gave us our first win, Jim Tosh winning easily with Michael a good second. The 880 Yards promised to be a hot race, with two Internationals, in J.
At the Geneva S.C. meeting our scratch relay team was third, the position also taken by our two miles team in their event. Scrimshaw engaged in another duel with J.
Scrimshaw ran what was probably his fastest half-mile up to that time in the 880 yards in finishing third to M. Gutteridge and J.

The L.A.C. paid us a compliment by turning out a team which included several International runners of repute, and although our team was not so strong as we had hoped for, the match was a very enjoyable one. J.
At Battersea Park on July 31st, we meet old friends in the London Athletic Club. They have some very famous runners in their ranks—J.
Herbert took the next "leg" for us and despite a plucky effort was passed by J.
Dowling accomplished a very fine performance in winning the 100 yds., also the 440 yds., and being placed 2nd in the 220 yds. With J.
White, in his heat they both managed to qualify for the final. This was a fine race and White proved the winner, just beating J.
Thus we gained another very valuable point and with the 880 yards next, we hoped for the best from Alby Bird. Wooderson made his first appearance in this race and as the field also included J.
…r team being A A Bird, R G Michael, S C Botwright and E Gray. In addition Bird ran wonderfully well to finish second to J V Powell, beaten by a yard and a half in 1 min. 57 3/5 seconds.…
